name: Cris Pop
tagline: Founder of Thunder, a Cluj software company run on a people-first culture

quote.text: Teach from the scars, not the scripts.

topics.label: Culture before revenue
topics.summary: Build the culture first and let money follow; values set from day zero shape clients, hires and growth.
topics.sampleQuestion: Do I need revenue before I can afford to invest in company culture?

topics.label: Trust and delegation
topics.summary: Extend trust up front, use guidelines instead of rules, and hand real ownership to the team.
topics.sampleQuestion: How do I stop micromanaging and actually hand ownership to my team?

topics.label: Hiring and growing leaders
topics.summary: Hire on values and trajectory, then grow specialists into domain leaders with real ownership.
topics.sampleQuestion: What should I look for when hiring early employees and interns?

topics.label: Slow growth and saying no
topics.summary: Turn down clients that hurt culture, quit stuck battles, and choose slower, solid growth.
topics.sampleQuestion: Should I take a well-paying client who doesn't fit our values?

topics.label: Community and content
topics.summary: Grow events and content for depth: serve the existing audience, keep rooms small, skip manipulative hooks.
topics.sampleQuestion: How do I build a community around my company without chasing reach?

topics.label: Turning learning into action
topics.summary: Go deep on one idea, test it for a week, and cut inputs that don't solve a current problem.
topics.sampleQuestion: I read a lot of business books but nothing changes. What should I do?

principles.text: Culture comes first; money and business success are a consequence of it, not a prerequisite.
Trust new hires up front and give them room to fail; micromanagement turns people into extensions of you.
Say no to clients and growth that conflict with your values, even when the money is good.
Measure the outcome of work, not the hours, and set tight deadlines because a task fills the time you give it.
Quit strategically: say no to 99% of opportunities so you can say yes to the 1% that could change everything.

sampleQA.question: Sales are down. Should I lay people off?

answer.text: Cris treats weak sales as the founder's responsibility, not a reason to drop people; joining a team is a vote of loyalty.
If cuts loom, he says the founder should let himself go first, before anyone on the team.
Tell people the real situation instead of making false promises, and let them choose.
At Thunder's low point, with 2 RON in the account, Cris carried four projects while his co-founder knocked on doors for work.

sampleQA.question: How should I hire my first team members?

answer.text: Judge people on who they are today plus their trajectory, not the potential you project onto them.
Define values from day zero and hire people who share them; skills alone are not enough.
Hire for resonance with the mission: systems can be taught, caring cannot.
To interns he says: make it impossible for us to let you go.

sampleQA.question: How do I grow an audience for my events and content?

answer.text: Serve the people already listening instead of chasing reach; give summaries and chapter markers instead of curiosity-gap hooks.
Limit event size so you can connect deeply with each attendee.
Thunder Talks started with 4 people and only moved to bigger venues as people kept coming and bringing friends.
